analysis:
Examined all supplied ProviderLoop excerpts, DaemonState coding changes and file metadata against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 detail. The complete range map limits ProviderLoop changes to lines 787–796: optional connection diagnostics and bookkeeping for unauthorized-connection recovery, including randomized jitter. DaemonState+Coding.swift adds an optional coding key at head line 18, decodeIfPresent at 51 and encodeIfPresent at 89; absent fields remain compatible. These additions alone neither grant serving permission nor change encryption, cache isolation, model validation, cancellation, billing or privileged-helper authority. No concrete regression is established in this scope.
Integration must examine ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery and the writers/resetters of ProviderLoop.swift:789–796: ensure reconnect recovery has bounded attempts/backoff, preserves in-flight cancellation and invalidates old connection grants without treating diagnostics as authorization (TB-002, TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-057). Also inspect DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection and its population/persistence paths to establish that the newly serialized field contains no credentials or unnecessary stable identifiers and reports trust accurately (A-008, T-058). Those implementations are outside the supplied source, so these are unverified contracts rather than findings. Existing SendHandle, process-key generation, model-slot ownership and cache-related state were examined as surrounding context, not attributed to this PR.
